audit.why: 45.02% over 502 games and the chart gives Ziggs six of seven stages with Rumble only Level 6. That is consistent, honest, and matches the kits — Bouncing Bomb at 850 versus Flamespitter at 600 is a permanent range deficit. The difficulty framing needed no change.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike calls Equalizer 'your only real leverage window' without saying what makes the window open. Nothing in the matchup is costed.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20/18/16/14/12 seconds. It is the only escape Ziggs has, and at rank 1 spending it leaves him with no mobility for twenty seconds — that, not the ultimate alone, is what makes the Level 6 kill real. Mega Inferno Bomb is 120/95/70 and Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16.
audit.corrected: Anchor the Level 6 spike to Satchel Charge's 20-second rank-1 cooldown rather than to the ultimate in isolation.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup treats Rumble as having no answer at range — 'his full kit reaches you while yours barely reaches him', 'you will never actually reach him'. Electro-Harpoon is 850 range. Bouncing Bomb is also 850. They are identical. Rumble is out-ranged on Flamespitter (600) and dead even on the harpoon, and the page never says so.
audit.why: Riot's data: Ziggs Q range 850, Rumble E range 850. Electro-Harpoon also carries two charges and shreds magic resist, so trading harpoons at max range is a real option in a lane the page currently describes as pure suffering. Naming the parity changes what the player does at level 2, which is the difference between farming under tower forever and contesting.
audit.corrected: State the 600-versus-850 deficit on Flamespitter and the 850-versus-850 parity on Electro-Harpoon, and tell the player to answer poke at his own range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. Every line is 'stay under tower' or 'you cannot win a fair trade' with no stated window in which you can.
audit.why: There is exactly one window and it is countable: bait Satchel Charge, then walk in during the twenty seconds before it returns. Without that number the matchup reads as unplayable rather than difficult.
audit.corrected: Add the explicit sequence — bait Satchel Charge with a harpoon, count twenty seconds, then commit Flamespitter.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ability is called 'Bounce Bombs' in wants.foe[0] and 'Bouncing Bombs' as a verb in mid. Riot's name is Bouncing Bomb, singular. Satchel Charge is likewise conjugated as 'Satchel Charges away'.
audit.why: The packet flagged five near-miss names here. 'Bounce Bombs' is a genuine fabrication; the pluralisations are looser but read as different abilities to a player scanning a loading screen.
audit.corrected: Use Bouncing Bomb and Satchel Charge as proper nouns throughout.

edits.before: This is a brutal opener. Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb out-ranges Flamespitter by a wide margin, meaning he can land poke on you before you can even begin generating Heat. Level 1 you are purely reactive — sit at the edge of the wave, eat as little bomb damage as possible, and do not walk up to try trading because you will not get in Q range before taking two bombs to the face. Level 2 you gain Electro-Harpoon, which is theoretically a slow to set up a close, but Ziggs has Satchel Charge at Level 2 as well and will simply knock himself away the moment your harpoon lands. Level 3 is more of the same: your full kit is online but Ziggs has his full kit too, and his full kit reaches you while yours barely reaches him. The only early kill threat you have is if he miscalculates his Satchel Charge direction and bounces toward you rather than away — play to punish that single mistake, not to win a fair trade.
edits.after: This is a brutal opener. Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 against Flamespitter's 600, so he lands poke on you before you can begin generating Heat. Level 1 you are purely reactive — sit at the edge of the wave, eat as little bomb damage as possible, and do not walk up to try trading, because you will not get into Q range before taking two bombs to the face. Level 2 changes more than it looks: Electro-Harpoon is also 850, so you can answer his poke at his own range and shred his magic resist instead of chasing him. He has Satchel Charge at Level 2 as well and will knock himself away the moment a harpoon lands — but that is 20 seconds at rank 1, and once it is spent he has no escape at all. Level 3 is the same shape with Hexplosive Minefield added on a flat 16-second cooldown. The only early kill threat you have is a mistimed Satchel Charge that bounces him toward you rather than away — play to punish that single mistake, not to win a fair trade.

edits.before: Level 6 is your one real foothold in this matchup. Equalizer fired across his retreat path — not at his feet, but the line he will walk to safety — can force a Flash or kill if he is already poke-damaged, and the threat of it alone makes him more cautious about stepping onto the wave to bomb. Use that psychological window to crash a wave and recall, or to shove and roam to a fight where your rocket wall is worth far more than any solo kill. Outside of Equalizer being up, Levels 4 through 5 are miserable: he zones you off the wave with Minefield planted on your approach, and every time you try to walk up with Flamespitter active he either Bouncing Bombs you from safety or Satchel Charges away before Q ticks deal meaningful damage. Stay under tower, soak what you can, and spend your mental energy tracking his roam timer rather than fighting a trade pattern you cannot win.
edits.after: Level 6 is your one real foothold in this matchup. Equalizer fired across his retreat path — not at his feet, but the line he will walk to safety — can force a Flash or a kill if he is already poke-damaged, and the threat of it alone makes him more cautious about stepping onto the wave to bomb. Use that window to crash a wave and recall, or to shove and roam to a fight where your rocket wall is worth far more than any solo kill. Outside of it, Levels 4 through 5 are miserable: Hexplosive Minefield zones your approach, and every walk-up with Flamespitter active ends with a Bouncing Bomb from safety or a Satchel Charge bounce before your Q ticks matter. The one sequence that works is baiting Satchel Charge with a harpoon, then counting the twenty seconds and walking your cone in on the back of it. Otherwise stay under tower, soak what you can, and track his roam timer instead.

notes: Of the five packet suspectNames, one was a genuine fabrication — 'Bounce Bombs' in wants.foe[0], corrected to Bouncing Bomb — and the rest were inflections ('Bouncing Bombs', 'Satchel Charges', 'Use Satchel Charge', 'Land Equalizer'); I rewrote the two used as verbs in mid and left the correct ones alone. The most useful thing this matchup was missing is not a name but a number: Electro-Harpoon and Bouncing Bomb are both 850 range, so the page's claim that Rumble can never reach him was overstated. Rumble's Scrap Shield carries spurious 'knockup' and 'terrain' derived flags, and the _missing-interactions 'terrain-cuts-retreat' entry claims Rumble can cut Ziggs's retreat with Scrap Shield and The Equalizer — Scrap Shield does neither, and The Equalizer slows rather than blocks, so I made no such claim. Satchel Charge also displaces Ziggs himself, which no wall would stop.
